title: Spire and Sigil
premise: In the city of Vhalen, where magic was outlawed after the Sundering War, Silas Kavanagh pays off his family's debt by selling harmless charms from a temple scriptorium. When a mute child arrives speaking the dead tongue of the pre-kingdom era, Silas discovers she carries a living sigil — the key to reopening the sealed Wellspring beneath the city. Hunted by both the Inquisitors who enforce the ban and the hidden Order that wants to weaponize the sigil, Silas and the child, Wren, find an unlikely ally in Captain Isolde Vey, the lawwoman ordered to capture them. As the Inquisitor-General moves to drain the Wellspring for himself, Silas must choose between destroying the sigil forever or trusting Isolde with a power that could corrupt them both; in the end they shatter it together, freeing magic back into the world rather than letting any one hand hold it.
about_author: Felix Nakamura is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval legal documents before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about ordinary people trapped inside systems larger than themselves, and lives quietly with two cats and an unreasonable number of fountain pens.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. We meet him hawking charms in Vhalen's rain-slick markets, counting coins against his family's crushing temple debt while Inquisitors patrol for illegal magic. A routine day ends when a barefoot child appears at his door at midnight, speaking words no living person should know. Beat: weary resignation cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Walls
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He realizes Wren's language matches glyphs in forbidden archive folios he has secretly copied for years. When an Inquisitor raid nearly catches them, Silas flees with the child into the undercity. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve as he chooses the child over his own safety.

chapters.title: Captain of Ash
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The Inquisitor-General orders her to hunt the scribe and the 'anomaly' child, promising her brother's pardon if she succeeds. She begins the chase dutifully, but reading Silas's confiscated ledgers unsettles her sense of what justice means. Beat: duty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: The Undermarket
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In the smugglers' warrens, Silas seeks a translator and instead finds the hidden Order of the Unquenched Flame, who claim Wren is a vessel of the Wellspring sigil. Their kindness feels rehearsed; their hunger for the child feels dangerous. Beat: suspicion blooming beneath gratitude.

chapters.title: What the Sigil Wants
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (rendered through sensation and image). The sigil stirs, showing her fragments of the Sundering War and whispering that it can end her loneliness forever. Silas, watching her sleepwalk toward the Order's altar, wrenches her away and runs. Beat: love asserting itself against seductive power.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Chains
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. She corners Silas and Wren on the aqueduct but hesitates when Wren speaks her dead brother's name in the old tongue. Silas offers her the truth instead of a fight: the Inquisitor-General intends to drain the Wellspring himself. Beat: the first crack in her loyalty to the law.

chapters.title: The General's Garden
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Isolde returns to headquarters and discovers the General's private vault of harvested magic — including relics taken from executed mages, perhaps her own family among them. She burns her warrant and sends a coded warning to Silas. Beat: betrayal transmuted into rebellion.

chapters.title: Nightfall Over Vhalen
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The Order, the Inquisition, and the General's private guard all converge on the Wellspring gate beneath the temple. Silas, Wren, and Isolde descend through collapsing tunnels as the city above erupts in panic. Beat: breathless flight toward the inevitable confrontation.

chapters.title: The Wellspring
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. At the sealed heart of the city, the General forces Wren to open the gate; the Order betrays everyone; the sigil offers Silas unlimited power to save them all. Instead he and Isolde shatter it together, releasing magic into the world unowned. Beat: sacrifice over dominion.

chapters.title: A City That Remembers
chapters.summary: Epilogue, shared POV. Months later, Vhalen reckons with returned magic: some rejoice, some grieve, laws are rewritten slowly. Silas's debt is annulled; Isolde helps found a new order of stewards rather than rulers; Wren finally speaks her own name aloud. Beat: hard-won hope, tender and unfinished.
